name: Hydra Host
snippet: Hydra Host runs Brokkr, software that provisions bare-metal GPUs across partner data centers, and sells that capacity to AI teams. It raised a $100M Series A in June 2026.
origin: CEO Aaron Ginn co-founded Hydra Host in 2021. TheNextWeb reports that the company started in crypto mining infrastructure and then moved into renting bare-metal GPUs for AI. It chose an asset-light model that connects independent data center owners with AI buyers instead of building its own sites.
today: Hydra Host closed a $100M Series A in June 2026, led by Kindred Ventures, with NVIDIA, ARK Invest, Comcast Ventures, Magnetar and PEAK6 among the new investors. TheNextWeb puts the valuation near $800M. The company says Brokkr manages more than 20,000 GPUs and runs in more than 50 partner data centers across the Americas, Europe and Asia. NVIDIA lists Hydra Host as a user of its DSX Air simulation tool for Brokkr development.
platform: Brokkr is an operating system for bare-metal GPU fleets that handles provisioning, out-of-band management, billing and lifecycle tasks through one API. Hydra also sells Confidential Metal for secure workloads. Its AI Factory Accelerator program helps hardware owners plan, finance and fill new GPU sites.
outlook: Hydra says it will spend the Series A on more GPU-as-a-Service capacity and international expansion. Supply deals such as Bitzero's 64-GPU B300 deployment in Norway, announced in January 2026, show how hardware owners use Brokkr to reach Hydra's buyers.

Massed Compute appears as a testimonial on the site and Bitzero is a supply-side Brokkr partner. The site says 40+ data centers while the June 2026 release says 50+, and I used the newer figure.

name: FarmGPU
snippet: FarmGPU is a small neocloud in Rancho Cordova, California that rents H200, B200 and RTX PRO 6000 GPUs. It builds clusters on open Ethernet networking and sells capacity directly and through RunPod.
origin: Jonmichael Hands, the CEO and co-founder, started FarmGPU as a sustainable GPU hosting business with a Tier 3 data center in Rancho Cordova, California. Its early model included tokenized GPU ownership through Berkeley Compute. In February 2025 it launched on RunPod Secure Cloud as the US-CA-2 region.
today: FarmGPU runs a 7 MW Tier 3 site in the US West and says it serves customers from multiple US locations. It brought up a 32-node B200 cluster in 17 days in late 2025 with Hedgehog fabric software and Celestica switches. In 2026 it published MLPerf Storage v3.0 results with Solidigm and WEKA and co-leads an Open Compute Project workstream on scaling AI clusters at neoclouds.
platform: FarmGPU offers on-demand and bare-metal NVIDIA servers with per-second billing and no egress fees. Its stack uses an 800G RoCEv2 Ethernet fabric, BlueField-3 DPUs, a custom TractorOS image and storage from VAST, WEKA and MinIO. It also co-runs the AI Central Lab with Solidigm for storage research.
outlook: FarmGPU says it plans to open-source its predictive failure engine for SSD fleets and to contribute benchmark and TCO data to OCP. Public sources give no figures for its funding or total GPU count.

name: PaleBlueDot AI
snippet: PaleBlueDot AI is a Palo Alto GPU cloud that runs its own clusters, a GPU marketplace and serverless inference. It raised $200M at a $3.2B valuation in October 2026.
origin: PaleBlueDot AI started in Silicon Valley in 2024 and takes its name from Carl Sagan's description of the Voyager photo of Earth. It began as a GPU cluster marketplace and added dedicated clusters for enterprise customers in colocation sites run by Digital Realty and Equinix. Stephen Watts became CEO in early 2026.
today: PaleBlueDot raised a $150M Series B led by B Capital in January 2026 at a valuation above $1B. In July 2026 it closed a $255M GPU-backed private note with Brookfield and Tor Investment Management. ComputeCore led a $200M Series C in October 2026 at a $3.2B valuation, and the company reports more than $5B in signed customer contracts. Customers in the US and Japan make up more than half of monthly revenue.
platform: The company runs self-owned GPU clusters, a marketplace for on-demand capacity from more than 25 supply partners, and a serverless inference service. Its HGX B300 cluster in Japan earned NVIDIA Exemplar Cloud status for large-model training in August 2026.
outlook: Bloomberg reported in September 2026 that PaleBlueDot is in talks with lenders including Brookfield for $600M of private credit to buy chips for a South Korea site used by Xiaohongshu. The company plans to use the Series C to add capacity and location options across North America, Japan, Korea and Southeast Asia.

name: Boost Run
snippet: Boost Run is a Northbrook, Illinois GPU cloud that listed on Nasdaq through a SPAC merger in May 2026. A $525.6M sovereign AI contract in October 2026 lifted its contract value above $2.6B.
origin: Andrew Karos founded Boost Run in 2023 and serves as CEO. The company launched its cloud services platform at the end of 2024. It places NVIDIA GPU servers in partner data centers, mainly TierPoint facilities, with Lenovo and Dell as hardware partners and Lumen for connectivity.
today: Boost Run combined with Willow Lane Acquisition Corp. on May 8, 2026 and trades on Nasdaq as BRUN. Q2 2026 revenue reached $31.1M, up 270% from a year earlier, and total contract value stood at $1.9B at the time. In October 2026 it signed a five-year, $525.6M agreement with an unnamed sovereign AI company for GB300 NVL72 systems, which took total contract value above $2.6B. The company runs six US data center locations and reports 253 MW of accessible power.
platform: Boost Run rents bare-metal NVIDIA GPU servers from A100 to B300 and takes reservations for GB300 and Vera Rubin capacity. It adds managed Kubernetes, CPU nodes, shared storage and private links to AWS, Azure and Google Cloud. It holds SOC 2 Type II, HIPAA, ISO 27001 and ISO 27701 certifications and is an NVIDIA Cloud Partner.
outlook: Boost Run targets about $400M in annual recurring revenue for 2026 and plans three new sites. It has fully committed a $1.44B Dell purchase agreement and plans $4B to $5B of further compute procurement. Acceptance of the first systems under the sovereign contract is expected in early Q2 2027.

name: VoltaCloud
snippet: VoltaCloud is an early-stage GPU cloud in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia that rents NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs. It is in a design partner phase with eight GPUs.
origin: VoltaCloud presents itself as a Saudi GPU cloud with local data residency, Arabic-language service and billing in Saudi riyals. Its site lists its commercial registration as in progress.
today: In October 2026 VoltaCloud offers eight NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs with 96 GB each in a Tier 3 data center in Riyadh. It is accepting design partners with limited capacity.
platform: Customers rent GPUs on demand or on reserved terms, with 100 Gbps networking and a 99.982% uptime SLA. The service states compliance with the Saudi Personal Data Protection Law and readiness for ZATCA e-invoicing.
outlook: VoltaCloud says it plans to expand its fleet through 2026.

name: Atlas Cloud
snippet: Atlas Cloud is a New York AI cloud that sells API access to more than 300 image, video, audio and language models alongside GPU clusters. It reported a fleet of over 20,000 GPUs in 2025.
origin: Jerry Tang founded Atlas Cloud and serves as CEO. The company launched as a neocloud that rented GPU clusters to AI startups and enterprises. By April 2025 it reported more than 20,000 GPUs across a global footprint.
today: In 2026 Atlas Cloud presents itself as a generative media platform with one API for more than 300 models. In April 2026 it opened ByteDance's Seedance 2.0 video model to developers with per-second billing and no waitlist. Its November 2025 partnership with EdgeUno brings NVIDIA H100 and H200 clusters to Sao Paulo, Bogota, Santiago, Buenos Aires and Mexico City.
platform: The platform combines model APIs for video, image, audio and language with GPU cloud capacity for custom workloads. Atlas Cloud reports SOC 2 Type II certification, HIPAA compliance and a 99.99% uptime SLA. It has staff in New York, Silicon Valley and Calgary.
outlook: Atlas Cloud and EdgeUno plan more multi-megawatt AI clusters in Latin America through 2027. Public sources give no funding total or 2026 GPU count for the company.

name: Argentum AI
snippet: Argentum AI is a San Francisco compute marketplace and AI cloud that signs capacity deals before it finances hardware. In 2026 it announced a $1.5B GB300 contract and a $2.5B, 300 MW data center deal.
origin: Founder and CEO Andrew Sobko built Argentum AI as a compute marketplace that connects buyers of GPU capacity with data centers and neoclouds that hold spare supply. In January 2026 the company described itself as an enterprise-grade compute marketplace and added Golf Saudi CEO Majed Al Sorour to its board.
today: In April 2026 Argentum AI announced a $1.5B agreement to provide about 10,500 NVIDIA GB300 GPUs to an unnamed AI company, plus two inference deals worth $140M and $100M. In May 2026 it signed a $2.5B framework with cloud company Boosteroid and real estate group DL Invest Group for 300 MW of AI data center capacity in Central and Eastern Europe. SiliconANGLE, citing Barron's, reported $7.8B in signed agreements by June 2026 and described Supermicro as a backer.
platform: Argentum sells Hardware-as-a-Service, Bare-Metal-as-a-Service and Platform-as-a-Service tiers on capacity it sources from partner operators and OEMs. The company says it secures power and customer commitments first, then arranges financing and hardware.
outlook: The company claims more than 200,000 available GPUs and a 3.3 GW power pipeline across nine or more live and contracted sites, without a public breakdown. The counterparties behind most of its large contracts and the sources of its financing are not public.

name: QumulusAI
aka: Global Digital Holdings, The Cloud Minders
snippet: QumulusAI is an Atlanta GPU cloud focused on inference that listed on Nasdaq in July 2026. In September 2026 it signed $240.9M of new three-year contracts for NVIDIA B300 capacity.
origin: QumulusAI traces back to two 2019 companies, WAHA Technologies and WAHA, Inc., which merged in December 2022 as Global Digital Holdings. In April 2025 the company acquired The Cloud Minders, a GPU-as-a-Service business it had first invested in in October 2023, and rebranded as QumulusAI. It adopted the name legally in August 2025 and still lists blockchain hosting facilities in Watonga, Oklahoma and Denton, Texas.
today: QumulusAI began trading on the Nasdaq Global Market as QMLS through a direct listing in July 2026. Q2 2026 revenue was $6.7M, up 118% from a year earlier, with AI compute at 84% of the total. The deployed fleet reached 3,088 GPUs, and cumulative signed contract value stood at $282.5M in August 2026. In September 2026 it added two three-year B300 contracts worth $240.9M with two inference platforms.
platform: QumulusAI rents NVIDIA GPU servers that range from H100 and RTX PRO 6000 to B200 and B300, and it lists GB300 NVL72 racks. It deploys capacity in colocation sites in metro Atlanta, Kansas City, Denver and Philadelphia and sizes each build to signed demand. It is an NVIDIA Cloud Partner.
outlook: The company guides to $300M of forward annual recurring revenue and 18 MW of capacity by the end of fiscal 2026. It also cites a line of sight to 2.5 GW by the end of fiscal 2027, against 8 MW under executed agreements in August 2026.

name: Corvex
snippet: Corvex is an Arlington, Virginia AI cloud that went public by merging into Nasdaq-listed Movano in March 2026. It plans to grow from about 1.5 MW to 8 MW of IT power by the end of 2026.

facts.label: IT power
facts.value: About 1.5 MW now, about 8 MW by end of 2026

origin: Seth Demsey and Jay Crystal co-founded Corvex in October 2024 to rent GPU infrastructure with a focus on security and confidential computing. In November 2025 Corvex agreed to an all-stock merger with Movano Inc., under which Corvex holders would own about 96% of the combined company. The two companies raised about $40M around the deal.
today: The merger closed on March 19, 2026, and Movano renamed itself Corvex, Inc. while keeping the MOVE ticker on Nasdaq. Corvex reported $3.8M of revenue in Q2 2026, and two customers accounted for 93% of it. In August 2026 it raised $33M in a private placement and announced about 3,000 new GPUs across a new Midwest site and an expanded Mid-Atlantic site, both due for service in Q4 2026.
platform: Corvex rents GPU servers, committed storage and virtual machines on shared CPU servers, with managed Kubernetes available. Its confidential computing service protects model weights inside hardware-enforced trusted execution environments on HGX B200 systems. In September 2026 it launched Token Factory, an inference API for open-weight models with zero data retention.
outlook: Corvex expects revenue from the new capacity to start in Q1 2027. A right of first refusal could take it above 20 MW by Q3 2027. The company says it is negotiating multi-year take-or-pay contracts for the new GPUs but has not announced signed customers for them.
